markdown_report:
The next experiment should isolate whether distinct historical corroboration improves the recurring-interest residual. At 20% progress, retain this small intervention and strengthen its controls before adding learned decay or another objective.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has 16.98% sampled training-pair reversals versus 1.91% for CDs_and_Vinyl; report categories separately, without treating these as validation estimates. (2) Feedback motivates recent, repeated interests, but establishes neither intent nor ownership. (3) Positive-offset pooling and downward-only clipping avoid amplifying weak evidence; confidence remains an operational support score, not a calibrated probability.

**Insights from related work.** (1) HGN and HAM already combine historical pooling, gating and reinforced interests; novelty rests on the explicit witness rule [4,5]. (2) TASTE motivates text modeling but uses pretrained components unavailable here; lexical overlap cannot establish sustained interest [1]. (3) CoDeR motivates distinguishing shifts from noise, subject to assumptions [2]. (4) Sampled evaluation can change model ordering; preserve the pinned selection objective [3].

**Framework and directions.** Cross evidence source (ID/lexical), temporal scope (recent/recurring), and intervention strength (normalized/confidence-preserving). Prioritize corroboration, magnitude calibration and shortcut controls. The branch is history-dependent; it does not require witnesses supporting each candidate directly. Compatibility and unmet needs remain unobserved.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a benefit and limitation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two-witness confidence residual [1,4,5] | 3/6/5 | O: explicit corroboration; P: falsifiable support mechanism; D: quadratic scan | O: close aggregation precedents; P: sparse-interest suppression; D: efficient deployment needs care |
| Learned recency decay [2] | 2/5/3 | O: targeted adaptation; P: adjustable timescale; D: one parameter/category | O: established technique; P: adds selection freedom; D: stability checks required |
| Matched whole-text shuffle [1,3] | 2/7/4 | O: task-specific control; P: exposes shortcuts; D: no encoder change | O: standard permutation principle; P: no direct accuracy gain; D: sparse matching strata |

**Selected algorithm.** Require two witnesses with identities different from each other and the anchor, separated by at least three retained positions. Confidence is the maximum minimum anchor–witness TF–IDF cosine within each causal prefix. Missing evidence yields zero. Compute exact prefix confidences using two distinct-label maxima, avoiding cubic enumeration. Pool recency-weighted ID embeddings with denominator one plus total weight; clip downward and add through a zero-initialized gate.

Prespecify baseline, starting residual and revised residual; prioritize matched recency-only pooling and shuffled-text controls within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Additional text, duplicate and synergy ablations remain budgeted follow-ups. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; report incomplete controls and selection uncertainty. Preserve training/export parity, four routes and diagnosis interfaces. No improvement is established.

[1] [TASTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029). [2] [CoDeR](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33379). [3] [Evaluation flaws](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf). [4] [HGN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09217). [5] [HAM](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034966/).

idea.description: Add a causal two-witness support residual to SASRec. Each historical anchor contributes only when two historical item identities, different from each other and the anchor, provide positionally separated lexical support. Confidence-weighted ID embeddings form a bounded residual retained during inference. Confidence denotes deterministic corroboration strength, not a calibrated probability. The residual represents history-level evidence; it does not enforce candidate-specific corroboration.
idea.motivation: The supplied feedback identifies isolated interactions and broad associations as possible sources of irrelevant recommendations. Requiring distinct witnesses operationalizes recurring lexical support without inferring ownership, unmet needs, compatibility, ratings or simulator traits. Distinct IDs are not statistically independent evidence: variants, duplicate descriptions and boilerplate can satisfy the rule. HGN and HAM substantially precede historical pooling and reinforced interests, so the contribution is a precisely specified support rule and controlled evaluation. No validation improvement or causal interpretation of user preferences is established.
idea.implementation_notes:
Fit category-specific, frozen TF–IDF on titles and descriptions of unique training-history items only. Concatenate title, a newline and description; replace absent fields with empty strings. Use sklearn TfidfVectorizer with lowercase=True, analyzer='word', token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b', ngram_range=(1,2), min_df=2, max_df=1.0, max_features=20000, sublinear_tf=True, use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True, norm='l2' and stop_words=None. Process fitting documents in ascending item-ID order. Transform other publicly available item text using this frozen transform; no held-out interactions or labels enter fitting. Empty documents map to zero; an empty fitted vocabulary disables the branch for that category. Serialize configuration, library version, vocabulary, IDF and item mapping beneath the trial directory. Keep the transformed item matrix sparse and avoid a dense catalog-by-catalog similarity matrix.

For each retained causal prefix ending at t, anchor j has confidence c[j,t] equal to the maximum of min(sim(j,k),sim(j,l)) across valid witnesses k<l<=t. Require three different item IDs for j,k,l and l-k>=3 in retained-event positions. All anchors must satisfy j<=t. Witnesses may precede or follow the anchor within the observed prefix; they need only be separated from each other. This precise rule does not require separation from the anchor. Spacing three and recency timescale twenty are fixed hypotheses, not established behavioral timescales. Nonnegative cosine and zero-vector handling make missing evidence contribute zero. Recompute support after truncation; no departing event may remain a witness. Use the baseline's retained events, padding and learned-position indexing. Positional ages and witness spacing use ranks among retained valid events, not timestamps or padding indices.

Compute all prefix confidences exactly in quadratic work after obtaining the sequence similarity matrix. For each anchor row a[q]=sim(j,q), scan right witness l in chronological order. Before querying l, insert k=l-3 when valid and its item ID differs from the anchor. Maintain the largest per-label maxima for two distinct item IDs, with their witness indices; update an existing retained label by its maximum, or compare a newly encountered label with the two retained entries. Two entries suffice because each query excludes only the right witness's label, with the anchor label already filtered. Query the largest retained maximum whose label differs from item[l], skip l when it equals the anchor ID, and update running_best with min(a[l], eligible_max). Save running_best as c[j,l] only when anchor j exists in that prefix. Missing eligible witnesses give confidence zero because similarities are nonnegative. Resolve equal maxima by ascending item ID and then earliest witness position. This is a direct algebraic consequence of max_k min(a[k],a[l])=min(max_k a[k],a[l]); the supplied streaming-extrema reference is background, not evidence for this exact labeled algorithm. Blocking cubic pair enumeration only reduces memory and is unnecessary here.

Each anchor scan is O(L), giving O(L²) scan work per sequence. The similarity matrix and stored confidence matrix require O(L²) memory; sparse cosine computation has additional feature-dependent cost. A naive Python loop over anchors, prefixes and batch elements can still be slow. Use batched tensor scans over the prefix axis, or precompute exact deterministic confidences for an explicitly fixed finite set of training windows. Do not assume GPU efficiency from asymptotic complexity. Profile the implementation and count profiling, diagnostics and failures against the shared budget. Compare the optimized scan with brute-force pair enumeration on small synthetic sequences before training. Do not silently introduce top-neighbor truncation or compressed text projections, which change the algorithm.

Set w[j,t]=c[j,t]*exp(-(t-j)/20), using retained-event ranks for t-j. Use the raw trainable item embedding table, without input dropout or the SASRec input sqrt(D) multiplier, for every pooling arm. Define p[t]=sum_j(w[j,t]*embedding[j])/(1+sum_j(w[j,t])). Define RMS(v)=sqrt(mean(v²)+1e-8), r[t]=p[t]*min(1,detach(RMS(base[t]))/RMS(p[t])). Return base[t]+tanh(alpha)*r[t], with one category-specific scalar alpha initialized to zero and padding outputs masked. Weak evidence is never scaled upward. Gradients flow through pooled embeddings and their norm, while the cap's base-feature norm is detached. The scalar gate can become negative; report its learned sign rather than interpreting it automatically as positive interest reinforcement. At initialization the branch gives baseline-equivalent features, its gate can receive gradients, and shared embeddings continue receiving baseline gradients. Preserve the baseline scoring convention identically during training and export.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200, original splits, four dataset routes and single-GPU execution. Keep baseline loss, optimizer and other settings for the first comparison. Do not assume a new sampler from the diagnostic loader's supplied negative items. Before executing trials, record the exact baseline settings, starting-residual configuration, checkpoint cadence, checkpoint selection rule, arm order and GPU-second allocations in a trial manifest. Those baseline details and measured runtimes are not supplied here, so a fully executable training reproduction cannot honestly be inferred from this report alone. Count every attempted configuration, failure, diagnostic and evaluation against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Do not reduce training allowance for controls after observing their scores.

Retain unchanged SASRec, the starting residual and the revised residual as the primary comparison. Use a matched recency-only residual with c=1 and otherwise identical denominator, cap, gate, embedding convention and training allowance to test whether corroboration contributes beyond pooling. Use a whole-text reassignment control, seeded at zero, within each dataset and joint strata defined by training-frequency decile, whitespace-token-count decile and metadata availability. Compute decile assignments using training-history items with stable item-ID tie breaking; leave singleton strata unchanged and report the fraction actually reassigned. Refit the same TF–IDF specification on the reassigned training documents for that arm. Nontraining items retain their public text and use the resulting frozen transform. This control is approximate because matching bins are coarse and singleton strata cannot be shuffled. Word-order shuffling is insufficient: it preserves unigram counts, although it can change the specified bigrams. Do not claim that all controls fit the budget before runtime accounting; identify incomplete comparisons explicitly.

Treat title-only, description-only, boilerplate-masked text, uniform pooling, most-recent-item similarity, HAM-style synergy, one-versus-two witnesses, relaxed identity constraints and duplicate handling as optional separately budgeted follow-ups. Define any duplicate detector, boilerplate-removal rule, additional hyperparameter and matching tolerance before using it. The Amazon documentation motivates auditing variants but does not establish their presence in these splits. Report descriptive training-text duplicate rates first; avoid inferring semantic independence from distinct IDs. Matched unrelated-user histories and position/order perturbations are auxiliary dependence probes, not substitutes for untouched benchmark histories or evidence of user causality. Text reassignment, history order and popularity controls answer different questions.

Use only the pinned host macro validation HR@10 for selection: 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Report each category and the unweighted macro mean as sampled-candidate outcomes. If the host exposes paired per-user hits, use 10,000 seed-42 bootstrap resamples independently within categories to estimate uncertainty in paired macro differences; retain checkpoint and candidate alignment. Otherwise omit intervals. These intervals do not cover training-seed variability or adaptive checkpoint/trial selection. Prespecify history-length and target training-frequency strata for descriptive reporting without subgroup tuning. Auxiliary full-catalog scores and twenty-user simulator judgments do not replace this objective. Do not access hidden test files, download external weights or acquire additional datasets.

Update the predictor writer to serialize and execute the same architecture, text mapping, masks, raw pooling embeddings, positional convention and retained-prefix computation. In evaluation mode, verify training-side and exported predictor score parity with identical checkpoints and candidates, using atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 for float32 calculations. Run checks for all four routes, repeated IDs, missing text, no eligible witnesses, ties, padding, one-event prefixes, truncated windows and all-padding inputs. Verify that removing events after a boundary leaves earlier features unchanged and that disabling the branch reproduces baseline features. Final scoring must use the baseline's final valid-position convention.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with view.model pointing to the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence) and predict_score(features, items) must expose the trained architecture; user_train, meta_data and review_data retain compatibility while unavailable fields remain unavailable. The loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Restore model modes and Python, NumPy, Torch and initialized CUDA RNG states after probes. Keep alignment and training-margin metrics descriptive rather than treating them as validated quality measures. Twenty real training users, five per category, receive full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for descriptive inspection only. Missing item categories, ratings, reviews, prices, stores, ownership and simulator traits must never be inferred or fabricated; compatibility claims require explicit title/description evidence and otherwise remain unknown.
idea.pseudocode:
Prespecify baseline configuration, arms, controls, checkpoint rule and accounted GPU budget
For each category:
    fit frozen TFIDF on unique training-history items in stable item-ID order
    serialize transform, sparse item-text matrix, item mapping and configuration
    initialize unchanged SASRec and scalar alpha = 0
    for sequence, positive, negative in baseline training batches:
        base = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
        gather retained valid events using baseline truncation and padding
        S = nonnegative_cosine(frozen_text(events)); zero missing-text similarities
        for each anchor j:
            top_two = empty distinct-label prefix maxima
            best = 0
            for right witness l in chronological event order:
                k = l - 3
                if k exists and item[k] != item[j]:
                    insert/update (item[k], S[j,k], k) in top_two
                if item[l] != item[j]:
                    v = largest retained maximum with label != item[l]
                    if v exists: best = max(best, min(v, S[j,l]))
                confidence[j,l] = best if j <= l else 0
        for each valid prefix ending at t:
            w[j] = confidence[j,t] * exp(-(t-j)/20), for j <= t
            pooled = sum(w[j] * raw_item_embedding(item[j])) / (1 + sum(w))
            rms_pool = sqrt(mean(pooled**2) + 1e-8)
            rms_base = detach(sqrt(mean(base[t]**2) + 1e-8))
            cap = min(1, rms_base / rms_pool)
            features[t] = base[t] + tanh(alpha) * cap * pooled
        mask padding features
        optimize unchanged baseline objective with features
    export identical architecture and feature computation through predictor writer
Verify exact scan against brute-force pairs and verify exported-score parity
Run prespecified comparisons and controls only within accounted shared budget
Select solely using pinned host macro validation HR@10
Report measured per-category outcomes, macro outcome, attempted trials and incomplete controls

originality.positive: The exact distinct-label, distance-constrained witness rule gives a precise and falsifiable alternative to additive historical evidence.
originality.negative: HGN and HAM already establish gating, historical pooling, multiple timescales and reinforced shared interests. The proposed branch is not candidate-specific corroboration, and novelty of its exact rule remains unverified.

future_potential.positive: Matched controls could establish when explicit support requirements improve history aggregation, motivating adaptive evidence thresholds and efficient corroboration operators.
future_potential.negative: Lexical duplicates, boilerplate and sparse histories may limit transfer. The method can suppress emerging interests and does not resolve practical compatibility, unmet needs or causal intent.

code_difficulty.positive: An exact quadratic scan removes cubic witness-pair enumeration, while the trainable modification remains one scalar around the existing encoder and embeddings.
code_difficulty.negative: Sparse text gathering, efficient batched scans, deterministic preprocessing, matched controls and predictor parity still require substantial integration. Quadratic work alone does not guarantee acceptable GPU runtime.

related_work.title: TASTE (CIKM 2023)
contributions: The supplied research summary describes text-based sequential recommendation through user–candidate text matching and sparse attention.
Reports long-tail and popularity-bias benefits, motivating tests of textual history information.
limitations: Its pretrained language-model components cannot be imported under this task's restrictions.
Does not establish that TF–IDF overlap or the proposed witness rule measures sustained interests.
Does not demonstrate gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: CoDeR (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary describes counterfactual modeling intended to distinguish demand shifts from noise.
Motivates separating transient evidence from persistent historical support.
limitations: Causal interpretations depend on modeling assumptions.
Lexical witness confidence alone does not identify demand shifts or user intent.

related_work.title: Hidasi and Czapp: Evaluation flaws in recommender systems research (RecSys 2023)
contributions: Documents that sampled and full-catalog evaluation can produce different model orderings.
Supports explicitly retaining the mandated sampled-candidate selection objective.
limitations: Does not supply evidence that the proposed architecture improves HR@10.
Auxiliary full-catalog diagnostics cannot replace the pinned host evaluation.

related_work.title: Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation (HGN, KDD 2019)
contributions: Combines long-term preferences, feature-level and instance-level historical gating, pooled preferences and historical-item–candidate interactions.
Provides close precedent for repeated-interest reasoning and gated aggregation.
limitations: Does not establish the value of the proposed fixed lexical, distinct-identity witness rule.
Its candidate-dependent historical evidence differs from this proposal's shared history residual.

related_work.title: HAM: Hybrid Associations Models for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines persistent preferences with pooled representations of longer and shorter recent histories.
Uses element-wise interactions to reinforce shared latent properties among historical items.
limitations: Creates substantial architectural precedent, limiting broad novelty claims for reinforced historical pooling.
Does not demonstrate that explicit lexical corroboration improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: Streaming maximum–minimum filter
contributions: Provides background on efficient streaming extrema computations.
limitations: Does not establish the exact distinct-label, distance-constrained witness query.
The proposed two-maxima scan requires its own algebraic justification and brute-force verification.

related_work.title: Amazon product data documentation
contributions: Documents near-identical product versions as a source of duplicated reviews in Amazon data.
Motivates auditing textual duplicates and variants as potential corroboration shortcuts.
limitations: Does not establish duplicate prevalence in the supplied RecHarness splits.
Provides background only; no additional dataset or review information may be imported.

related_work.title: Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns in Sequential Recommendation
contributions: The supplied summary distinguishes sequence patterns arising from user behavior and item availability.
Motivates interpreting temporal perturbations separately from semantic controls.
limitations: Unconstrained history shuffling may change availability relationships and introduce distribution shift.
Survival under shuffling does not establish causal user preferences or unobserved traits.
